fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Real past lives or the mind's stories?", "body": "Chance lays out three ways to read regression material: a linear chain of lives, one shared consciousness that has lived every life, or the unconscious inventing a symbolic answer when a therapist prompts it. Shelley says each has some validity. She personally believes in reincarnation but treats regression as a process, asks open-ended questions to avoid leading, and cares less whether a memory is a real life, an archetype or something seen on the Discovery Channel than whether it brings healing to the present. She says historical verification has not been part of her practice, while Chance points to reported cases of children in India recalling previous families."}, {"title": "The RELIEF method and the future self", "body": "Shelley coined the acronym RELIEF for the process she has used with clients for about twenty years. She compares it to pulling a weed by the root instead of mowing it: find the source event, cut the cords to unwanted influences, often with a guide such as Archangel Michael, then lift the memory with light and frequency. The last step takes the client into a happier future, the one place she says she deliberately leads. Chance likens this to setting an anchor that later choices are drawn toward, a link he ties to Dean Radin's work, and the book gives readers scripts to record and replay."}, {"title": "Pain, silence and staying grounded", "body": "Asked why negative emotions have to be felt, Shelley says pain may not be strictly necessary, but people tend to do the work only once discomfort turns into pain they cannot ignore. She describes ten days of silence at a Vipassana retreat south of Dallas, where sitting still with discomfort echoed what she says Buddhists teach, that thoughts are forms carrying karma from past lives. Chance recalls a stranger handing him black tourmaline and walking him through grounding, and Shelley, who says many people are empaths, leads listeners through a brown grounding light sent down through the feet into the core of the earth."}, {"title": "Karma, patterns and chosen challenges", "body": "Shelley says some people wear their karma openly while others hide it, and that clients usually find several past lives where they repeated the same pattern, which she believes can end once it is recognised. She suggests lives spent in survival mode left little room for that reflection, and floats the idea, controversial by her own account, that souls sign up for some hardships before birth, which she uses as a tool for empowerment rather than victimhood. Chance takes a middle view, and in his outro warns that belief in chosen suffering must never become an excuse for mistreating other people."}, {"title": "Imagination as a source of real answers", "body": "Shelley calls imagination critical to regression and to life, asking readers of Meet Your Karma to record her scripts, play them back and trust the first random thought that floats up, much as they would a dream image; she says the client supplies every answer from the higher self. Chance, calling himself a philosophical idealist, argues that all thinking and perception are forms of imagination, and in his outro says visualization improves with practice. He then describes recording Shelley's exercises for his own self-guided regression, meeting a guide in the form of Gandalf and glimpsing what felt like a life in medieval France."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Dr. Shelley Kaehr is the author of several books, and in this episode we discuss her newest: Meet Your Karma: The Healing Power of Past Life Memories. As an experienced hypnotic regression therapist and energy healer, Dr. Kaehr is a timeline technician who helps clients find relief from trauma, compulsions, and soul contracts that sometimes hide in our unconscious minds. This interview explores theories about karma & reincarnation, the lessons we receive from pain and discomfort, and example cases from Shelley's practice with clients.
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "We're lazy people, and sometimes we just won't do the work unless it starts to hurt.", "author": "Shelley Kaehr", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "When you shift your perspective, expand your awareness and see that your experiences in the world are mirrors of your innermost self, you can elevate past the suffering of life's many causes and effects.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "I don't believe that a human being in this current reality that we are in as a physical being can consciously understand the vastness of this universe completely.", "author": "Shelley Kaehr", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "What's weird about life is that some people are wearing their karma and their emotional strife right out on their shirtsleeve, where everybody can see it.", "author": "Shelley Kaehr", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "Imagination isn't a type of thinking. All forms of thinking and all forms of perception are actually types of imagination, or ways of imagining.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "If I caused it, then maybe I can do something about it, and I can change it.", "author": "Shelley Kaehr", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "Letting go of what other people think about us has nothing to do with walking all over people or doing whatever we want at the expense of anybody else.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "I think that the answers really are within ourselves if we can quiet ourselves down enough to receive those answers.", "author": "Shelley Kaehr", "portrait": ""}]
